key_insight: MonoArt progressively decouples object structure from motion cues so a single image suffices to recover articulated 3D shape and joint parameters, stabilizing articulation estimation without multi-view or video supervision.
problem_solved: Addresses the instability and entanglement between motion cues and object structure in monocular articulated 3D reconstruction, avoiding reliance on multi-view data, retrieval-based assembly, or auxiliary video generation.
method: Progressive structural reasoning: infer coarse part graph first, then refine part geometry and joint parameters in staged steps to reduce ambiguity.
Decoupling of structure and motion: learn articulation-aware representations that separate pose/motion regression from part geometry estimation for more stable optimization.

Single-image, scalable pipeline: end-to-end trainable model that reconstructs articulated 3D objects from one view using learned priors and iterative refinement rather than heavy multi-view or retrieval data.
impact: Enables efficient, scalable monocular reconstruction of articulated objects for downstream tasks (robotics, AR/animation) by removing the need for multi-view captures or costly retrieval/video pipelines, making 3D articulation more practical in real-world settings.

paper_title: MonoArt: Progressive Structural Reasoning for Monocular Articulated 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Haitian Li, Haozhe Xie, Junxiang Xu, Beichen Wen, Fangzhou Hong
